ShortDescription.Value: Ski resorts: lifts that fit your terrain, runs on natural or machine-made snow, lodges, ski school and patrol, a resort planner, resort economics, and merging your own buildings.

Publish.LongDescription:
[Trailer](https://youtu.be/NJvzaxwGfa4) | [Features](https://youtu.be/mkysRTD0zmQ)
**Build a ski resort in Cities: Skylines II.**
Draw lifts up your mountain and runs down it. Natural or machine-made snow opens the runs. Guests ski (counted, not shown, yet), buy tickets and lessons, and the resort draws tourists to your city. No mods required, but Anarchy and Move It are highly recommended, along with Write Everywhere.
## Highlights - **Four lifts, one tool.** Fixed-grip triple chairlift, detachable quad chairlift, gondola and aerial tram. The tool plans numbered towers over your terrain, and you can move them. Chairs and cabins ride the rope. - **Runs on real snow.** Groomed or natural, with floodlights. Snow guns build a 2 m base that keeps a run open through a thaw. Each run is rated from its hardest pitch, in North American or European grading. It opens at 3 ft (91 cm) of snow on 60 % of the run. - **Night on the mountain.** Floodlights come on at dusk, like the street lights. Groomers work the cat tracks from dusk to dawn. - **Resort Planner.** Outline a mountainside and get a plan of linked runs, cat tracks and lifts. - **Seasons.** Snow melts in spring, runs close, and chairlifts and gondolas stop. Lodges and the school close off-season. The aerial tram keeps running for summer sightseeing. Northern and Southern Hemisphere maps both work. - **Lodges, Ski School, Ski Patrol and a Ski Bus Depot.** Five lodges, a school, two patrol buildings, and a coach stop in town for a hill too far away. - **Merge your own buildings.** A landmark, signature or recreation building near the runs can join the resort as a lodge. - **One hub.** Attraction, runs, lifts, guests, finances and history, with every problem and its cause. - **A resort economy.** Tickets, season passes, lessons and lodge spend against running costs. Set the ticket and season pass prices with sliders in the hub. To raise ticket tolerance, build better lodges. The resort tourism bonus raises the whole city's attractiveness, as an airport does.
## Requirements Cities: Skylines II 1.6 (tested on 1.6.4f1). No DLC or other mod required.
## Getting started Open the Ski Resort hub (button at the top left). Its Start card lists the four steps to a first resort.
## Good to know - Skiers are counted, not visually simulated. Chairs and cabins move but carry no riders. (Post Park Adventures, I will try my best to at least get Cims on the chairlifts) - Lifts are built on the game's power-line network, so the game shows some power-line details for them, such as a Transformer section in station panels. Like a real lift, each base station needs low-voltage power. The game refuses a high-voltage line at a lift. - The Mountain Hut, Chalet and Summit lodges, both patrol buildings, the Ski School and the fixed-grip and tram top stations keep the slope they stand on. Build them into the hillside with the terrain tools or Move It. - Bulldozing a Welcome Sign deletes every run linked to it and refunds no run fee. A warning comes first. - Two lifts of the same type cannot cross. A cat track cannot pass under a lift that is already built, so build cat tracks first. - Before uninstalling, use "Delete all ski resort content" in the mod's Options, then save the city. - Resorts cost money all year and earn in winter. Welcome to ski resort economics!
## Guides and details - [Docs site](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort): guides, every number, settings and troubleshooting. - Start with the [Resort Quickstart](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/quickstart/) and the [Lifts guide](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/guides/lifts/). - Bug reports: the [Paradox forum thread](https://forum.paradoxplaza.com/forum/threads/modular-ski-resort.1949673/) or the [Discord thread](https://discord.com/channels/263634513861541888/1570379334672326736). Paste the text from the Copy diagnostics button in the mod's Options. - [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/theotherwildcathighboy/ModularSkiResort)
## Credits - Modular Golf Course Pack by joergeske: the modular recreation idea this mod grew from. - Meapy's Tourism Overhaul: studied for how tourism and attractions work. Not required. Works alongside this mod. - Logo and in-game icon by [Lexa](https://lexakeenen.com/). - All assets (chairs, lodges, patrol huts) are based on [real places](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/credits/#asset-inspirations). - Built with Claude (Anthropic) for decompilation, prefab work and asset generation. Direction and many, many hours of testing by the author. - [Full credits and licenses](https://theotherwildcathighboy.github.io/ModularSkiResort/credits/).
Publish.ChangeLog:
**Season passes:** - Passes go on sale before the winter and sell for four months. The price rises 15 % halfway through. - Sales end in the fifth month of the season. Guests who first arrive after that pay day tickets. - Tourists can now ski on a destination pass. They pay a reduced day fee, never skip a ski day over the price, and the fee counts as pass income. - The Finances view shows how long passes stay on sale, and the destination fee with the share of tourists on a pass. - Pass texts in the Finances and Guests views are reworded ("On a pass", "Season passes sold").
**Lift tickets:** - Tourist groups that the game sends on outings now react to the ticket price. Above the default ticket some walk away, about half at the highest ticket. - The Guests view counts them as "Turned away by price".
**Lodges:** - Lodge spending now follows the ticket price, damped: a higher ticket brings more per guest, but less than the ticket rises. At the default ticket nothing changes.
**History:** - A revenue chart in the season block: income and costs by part on one scale, the net gap between them, and the pass share of lift income. Each part has a tooltip.
**Behind the scenes:** - The mod now carries its real version number (1.0.3) instead of 1.0.0, so Skyve and the game show the right version. - Saves from 1.0.0 to 1.0.2 load as before.
